# Phase 2: Control Extraction & Mapping

### 🎯 Objective
This phase translates the theoretical compliance requirements identified in the Product Fruits SOC 2 Type 2 report into a practical, technical audit program. By mapping the original AWS native controls to a Microsoft Azure and GitHub architecture, this framework demonstrates how "Compliance as Code" is actively enforced and audited in a modern cloud environment.

### 🗺️ Methodology
The following Risk Register and Audit Program bridges the gap between GRC policy and cloud engineering. It takes the formal Trust Services Criteria (TSC) from the SOC 2 report, identifies the inherent business risk, assigns the specific Azure technical control, establishes the automated GitHub enforcement mechanism, and defines the exact testing procedure an IT auditor would use to verify compliance.

---

### 🛡️ Cloud Native Risk Register & Audit Program

| SOC 2 Criteria & Policy | Identified Business Risk | Azure Technical Control | GitHub Enforcement Mechanism | Auditor Verification Test |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Logical Access (CC6.1, CC6.3, CC6.6)**<br>Access to critical systems requires Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and least privilege routing[cite: 1]. <br><br>*(Source Location: Section 3 Logical Access; Testing Matrix Control CC6.6.1)*[cite: 1] | Unauthorized threat actors bypass weak credentials to gain global administrative rights and compromise the cloud tenant. | Enforce **Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access Policies** requiring MFA for all administrative roles. Implement strict **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** via custom roles. | Securely store Azure service principal credentials within **GitHub Actions Encrypted Secrets**. Restrict deployment execution to approved environment administrators. | **Inspection & Inquiry:** Inspect the Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs and active role assignments to verify MFA enforcement and absence of standing Global Admin privileges. |
| **Change Management (CC8.1)**<br>All production code changes must undergo peer review by a person other than the author[cite: 1]. <br><br>*(Source Location: Section 3 Change Management; Testing Matrix Control CC8.1.4)*[cite: 1] | Unverified vulnerabilities, malicious code, or misconfigurations are pushed directly to production, causing system outages. | Implement **Azure Policy** to explicitly block manual infrastructure modifications in the portal, forcing all changes through automated pipelines. | Configure **Branch Protection Rules** on the `main` branch. Require passing status checks and at least 1 approving peer review, strictly blocking authors from approving their own pull requests. | **Observation & Inspection:** Sample a selection of closed pull requests merged during the audit window to verify the approving reviewer identity differs from the code author. |
| **Data Encryption (CC6.7)**<br>Data at rest must be encrypted using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) 256-bit[cite: 1]. <br><br>*(Source Location: Section 3 Cryptography; Testing Matrix Control CC6.7.2)*[cite: 1] | Physical storage disks or database backups are intercepted, exposing unencrypted Customer Confidential information. | Enable Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) on **Azure SQL / Cosmos DB** using customer-managed keys securely housed within **Azure Key Vault**. | Embed infrastructure as code scanning tools (e.g., Checkov, TFSec) directly into the **CI/CD workflow** to automatically block deployments of unencrypted data stores. | **Inspection:** Inspect the production Azure configuration blueprints and storage account encryption settings to verify AES-256 cryptographic enforcement. |
| **Vulnerability Management (CC7.1)**<br>The entity identifies vulnerabilities through the execution of regular vulnerability scans[cite: 1]. <br><br>*(Source Location: Testing Matrix Control CC7.1.3)*[cite: 1] | Unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in the application runtime are exploited by external attackers to exfiltrate data. | Deploy **Microsoft Defender for Cloud** to continuously assess virtual machines, container registries, and app services for known CVEs. | Enable **Dependabot** and **GitHub Advanced Security** secret scanning to automatically detect vulnerable dependencies and exposed API keys at the repository level. | **Observation:** Observe the Microsoft Defender for Cloud dashboard and GitHub security alerts tab to verify that regular scans are running and high severity findings are tracked. |
| **Availability & Backups (A1.2)**<br>Data backups are maintained daily and restored at least annually to verify integrity[cite: 1]. <br><br>*(Source Location: Section 3 Availability; Testing Matrix Control A1.2.2 & A1.2.3)*[cite: 1] | A catastrophic regional data center failure or accidental deletion permanently destroys the primary production database. | Configure the primary database and storage accounts for **Geo-Redundant Storage (GRS)** and enable automated daily backups to an **Azure Recovery Services vault**. | Define and deploy the backup retention policies programmatically via version-controlled **Infrastructure as Code (IaC)** templates. | **Inspection:** Inspect the Azure Recovery Services vault job logs to verify daily backup success and review the documentation from the annual disaster recovery restoration exercise. |
